newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dehaene slams Renault closure ahead of Chirac visit.
newsitem.headline: Dehaene slams Renault closure ahead of Chirac visit.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, speaking ahead of a visit by French President Jacques Chirac, said on Wednesday that Renault's closure of a car plant had been announced with "19th century" disregard for staff.
Dehaene singled out disputes with France over the closure of the Renault plant in Belgium employing 3,100 people, and French refusal so far to hand over secret documents in a bribery case.

"The way this decision was taken and announced in the (Renault) company was totally unacceptable and more in line with labour relations of the 19th century than the 20th or the 21st centuries," Dehaene told France-Inter radio.

But he struck a conciliatory note, saying of talks with former French Prime Minister Alain Juppe: "The position which he explained to me was the position that I would have defended if I was in his place. He told me that the company's autonomy was at stake, and that he must respect this."
The French state is the biggest shareholder in Renault with 46 percent.
Dehaene, due to meet Chirac after his arrival on Wednesday afternoon, urged France to hand over secret documents for Belgium's bribery probe against French warplane maker Serge Dassault.

"Both France and Belgium defend within the European Union the idea of a unified judicial area. The sending of the documents should take place in a more flexible way than it is happening now," Dehaene said.

Belgian police are investigating allegations that Dassault Aviation paid 600 million Belgian francs ($17 million) to political parties to secure a contract to fit air defence systems to Belgian F-16 jets in the late 1980s.
France's former centre-right government refused to hand over the documents but the new leftist government of Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has said it is reviewing the request.
